question.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =-2$ and $\sigma =3.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-5.9<X<-2.84) & =P(\frac{-5.9-(-2)}{3}<Z<\frac{-2.84-(-2)}{3}) \\  & =P(-\frac{3.9}{3}<Z<-\frac{0.84}{3}) \\  & =P(-1.3<Z<-0.28).\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/2552771608864efdcc2d8e867320d825b5f2297f24553acb0d8ecc92d3b4908e.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.3<Z<-0.28) & =P(Z<-0.28)-P(Z\le -1.3) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.28)-P(Z\le -1.3) \\  & =Φ(-0.28)-Φ(-1.3).\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-1.3) & =0.0968 \\ Φ(-0.28) & =0.3897\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.3<Z<-0.28) & =Φ(-0.28)-Φ(-1.3) \\  & =0.3897-0.0968 \\  & =0.2929.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(-5.9<X<-2.84)=0.2929.
$$
